title: Cascaded prostate-MRI model shows limited lesion detection and classification in clinical testing
summary: A cascaded 3D U-Net and residual-network system was evaluated on held-out clinical prostate MRI scans, with partial targeted-biopsy comparison. It detected 56.1% of expert-marked lesions and achieved 30.8% overall PI-RADS classification accuracy. The result documents limitations of retrospective clinical performance, without established cancer-screening benefit or evidence that the system can replace biopsy.
ai_technology: Cascaded 3D U-Net lesion segmentation and 3D residual networks for BPH filtering and PI-RADS classification
organization: National Cancer Institute; National Institutes of Health; NVIDIA

evidence.tested: The source reports 150 held-out scans with 198 expert-marked lesions. After benign-hyperplasia filtering, the algorithm detected 111 of 198 lesions, with PPV 62.7% and overall PI-RADS accuracy 30.8%. Among 136 lesions with targeted biopsy, 82.3% of detected reference lesions were tumor-positive, while 50.9% of missed reference lesions were benign. This is a specific clinical evaluation with partial pathology follow-up, beyond a public image benchmark alone.
evidence.unknown: Detection/reference categories were defined by one expert radiologist rather than complete histopathology. False-positive regions lacked targeted-biopsy validation, preventing full cancer detection-rate assessment. Cohort totals are supported by Figure 1, but abstract/Methods split counts conflict; pathology-grade subtotals also do not fully reconcile. Prostate-X includes repeated scans, and individual-patient separation across all partitions was not reconstructed. No reader-assistance benefit, prospective workflow evaluation or clinical efficacy was demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Learned networks detected and classified suspicious regions from patient MRI; comparison with expert labels and available biopsy outcomes produced the represented diagnostic-validation result. Low performance is retained rather than treated as evidence of clinical utility.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary clinical cohort, expert reference, cascaded 3D U-Net/residual architecture and hold-out evaluation Methods; test detection/classification, partial biopsy Results and limitations. Directly viewed Figure1; split-count and pathology-grade discrepancies preserved. Supplements and individual scans not independently reconstructed. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
